name: Ithaka 2
content: *To be read alongside “Ithaka” by CP Cavafy*

Laistrygonians, Cyclops, angry Poseidon—I was not afraid. Rare excitements stirred my spirit and my body but my soul set them up in front of me. I was unfamiliar with them. They’d called before I set out and so I took all the necessary ointments but I’d never seen their faces, never felt them breathing down my chest. Laistrygonians, Cyclops, wild Poseidon—they are welcome guests, and frankly to be expected if you wish to wed, in the Garden of Eden. If you don’t invite them they will crash the buffet and drink all your whisky, and for a while they will have a run of the place. You may be stripped anew; better maybe if you are Theseus’s than overnight, or perhaps not. And it is going to be alone at first. You can surround yourself but one night on the walk back it will find you. But there will be Phonecian strangers. Very likely they will be sellers of a sort but they will be kind. Buy their perfumes: when in Rome. And make friends with them; you will see them again. Do not forget to look around while seas are calm. There will be golden, pink, baby blue, fluffy white, all in shades and tones, and sights only for the sorest of eyes. Go out of your way to seek beauty and love, and take scenic detours: better if it lasts for years. Let snow into that solemn window, and lay beneath the comforter of love so you don’t get cold. Let snow into that solemn window, and lay beneath the comforter of love so you don’t get cold.
